source.citation: Hawkins, May, Pickett and Abell (1991), Benefits of NOAA-11 Channel #3 in Detection of Mesoscale Eddies in the Gulf of Mexico During Summer, pp. 356–360, in Proceedings: Eleventh Annual Gulf of Mexico Information Transfer Meeting, November 1990. OCS Study MMS 91-0040, published October 1991.
source.access: Original proceedings PDF acquired; actual PDF pages 345–347 / printed pages 356–358 reviewed. Authors explicitly identify Quiet in the same discussion. The dimensions are printed source approximations from August 12 and 19 imagery, not OSW graph or map readings.

interpretation: The author description of the elliptical SST feature is retained as source-reported approximate axis lengths. No exact per-image axis pairs, mathematical ellipse fit, threshold contour, uncertainty distribution or seasonal range are supplied. Nearly is an approximate-language qualifier, not a strict numeric upper bound.

additional_sources_reviewed.decision: Bosphorus is explicitly labelled in model Figure 10, but circulation arrows merge into adjacent flow and no objectively isolated edge was established. No size admitted.

additional_sources_reviewed.source: Hamilton et al. (2015), Observations and Dynamics of the Loop Current, BOEM 2015-006
additional_sources_reviewed.decision: Named historical charts are useful primary-context leads, but fronts, drifter paths, masking and feature connectivity were not resolved sufficiently for new individual dimensions. No generic line bounds or whole-eddy sizes admitted.

additional_sources_reviewed.source: Biggs, editor (1991), TIGER/AMIGO cruise 91G-02 technical report 91-02-T
additional_sources_reviewed.decision: Explicit Quiet identification and March 1991 survey/NOAA archive metadata retained as a future hydrographic lead. No raw station values, cruise averages, or warm-patch bounds promoted to size.
